Q1.answer:
There are 10 presidential documents in the series. For each I give the proclamation number, FR Doc. number, first FR page, date signed, date published, what it does, and the time its operative change applies.

**Duty proclamations** (each imposes a 50% ad valorem duty on its Annex II products):
1. **Proc. 11046 (alcoholic beverages)**, FR Doc. 2026-14991, 91 FR 46639. Signed Jul 20, 2026; published Jul 23. Printed start: 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 19, 2026. Measured against: entry for consumption or withdrawal from warehouse for consumption.
2. **Proc. 11047 (dairy)**, FR Doc. 2026-14992, 91 FR 46653. Signed Jul 20; published Jul 23. Same printed start (Aug 19) and same event.
3. **Proc. 11048 (motor vehicles)**, FR Doc. 2026-14997, 91 FR 46663. Signed Jul 20; published Jul 23. Same printed start (Aug 19) and same event.

**Delay:**
4. **Proc. 11056**, FR Doc. 2026-17294, 91 FR 54789. Signed Aug 18; filed Aug 21; published Aug 24. It moves the start of all three duties to 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 22, 2026, measured against the same entry/withdrawal event. It contains no separate effective date of its own and changes no products.

**Import bans** (each bans its Annex products from importation):
5. **Proc. 11061 (alcohol)**, FR Doc. 2026-18835, 91 FR 58311. Signed Sep 8; published Sep 14. Applies to goods imported on or after 12:01 a.m. ET Sep 29, 2026, so it is measured against importation, not entry. Goods imported but not yet entered before Sep 29 stay subject to the 50% duty.
6. **Proc. 11062 (dairy)**, FR Doc. 2026-18836, 91 FR 58319. Same dates; same importation test.
7. **Proc. 11063 (motor vehicles)**, FR Doc. 2026-18837, 91 FR 58325. Same dates; same importation test.

**Scope changes:**
8. **Proc. 11064 (alcohol)**, FR Doc. 2026-18838, 91 FR 58331. Signed Sep 8; published Sep 14. Annex I Part A products become dutiable; Part B products are removed; the duty now applies on top of section 232 duties. Applies from 12:01 a.m. ET Sep 15, 2026, measured against entry or withdrawal.
9. **Proc. 11065 (motor vehicles)**, FR Doc. 2026-18839, 91 FR 58339. Signed Sep 8; published Sep 14. Same structure and same Sep 15 start.
10. **Proc. 11076 (motor vehicles, further change)**, FR Doc. 2026-22292, 91 FR 68861. Signed Oct 23; filed Oct 29 at 11:15 a.m.; published Oct 30. The parts are reversed here: Part A products are **removed** and Part B products are **added**. The section 232 stacking is restated. Applies from 12:01 a.m. ET Oct 30, 2026, measured against entry or withdrawal.

**Which documents changed which products are subject to the duty:**
- **Alcoholic beverages:** 11046 (Annex II); 11064 (Part A added, Part B removed, and section 232 articles brought in from Sep 15); 11061 (moves its Annex products from the duty to the ban for goods imported from Sep 29).
- **Dairy:** 11047 only, plus 11062 (moves its Annex products from duty to ban). No dairy scope proclamation has been published.
- **Motor vehicles:** 11048; 11065 (Part A added, Part B removed, section 232 stacking from Sep 15); 11076 (Part A removed, Part B added from Oct 30); 11063 (ban).
- **Proc. 11056** changed only timing.
Q1.uncertainty:
- The annex product lists are images and cannot be read.
- The Federal Register search found no CBP notice modifying the HTSUS for these actions, and no dairy scope proclamation, even though Proc. 11062 cl. (3) refers to one.
- Proc. 11056 states no effective time of its own; it presumably operated from signing (Aug 18), which was before it was filed (Aug 21) and published (Aug 24).

Q2.answer:
**(a) Section 338 duty on each entry:**
- Entry 1 (2:00 p.m., Aug 20): **$0**. It is before 12:01 a.m. Aug 22.
- Entry 2 (11:59 p.m., Aug 21): **$0**. Still before 12:01 a.m. Aug 22.
- Entry 3 (12:01 a.m., Aug 22): **$40,000 × 50% = $20,000**. 'On or after 12:01 a.m.' includes 12:01 a.m. itself.
- Controlling text: Proc. 11056 cl. (1): 'The effective date of the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048 shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026.' Proc. 11046 cl. (1) supplies the trigger: goods 'entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after' that time.

**(b) How the start date was changed:**
- Proc. 11056 cl. (1) did two things. It declared the new effective date, and it amended 'the chapeau of Annex II' of each of the three proclamations by replacing 'August 19, 2026' with 'August 22, 2026'.
- It did **not** amend the body text. Clauses (1) and (3) of 11046 (91 FR 46641), and recital 9 (46640), still print 12:01 a.m. Aug 19.
- The difference is resolved by three things:
  - the first sentence of 11056 cl. (1), which fixes the effective date directly;
  - 11056 cl. (5), under which any inconsistent provision of a previous proclamation 'is superseded to the extent of such inconsistency';
  - later recitals confirming the duties took effect Aug 22 (e.g. 11061 recital 4, 91 FR 58311).

**(c) Getting back the deposit on entry 1:**
- Proc. 11056 cl. (2) directs agencies to 'suspend the collection' of the duties 'as soon as practicable'.
- 11056 cl. (4): 'To the extent that implementation of this proclamation requires a refund of duties collected, refunds shall be processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds.'
- 11056 was published Aug 24 (filed Aug 21), after entry 1, so a deposit could have been collected. No specific refund procedure is named.

**(d) Was further presidential action needed?**
- No. 11056 itself set the new date. No later document was needed for the duties to begin.
- Later recitals tell the story: Canada had expressed a commitment to remove the discrimination (11056 recital 4). On Aug 21, 2026 Canada 'reneged on its commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith'. At 12:01 a.m. Aug 22 'the 3-day suspension ... lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties ... became effective'. See recitals 2–4 of 11061 (58311), 11064 (58331) and 11076 (68861).
- These are recitals, not operative text.

**(e) Why the original date was Aug 19:**
- Section 338, as recited in 11046 recital 10 (46640–41), bars duties from taking effect 'earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation'.
- Signed Jul 20 + 30 days: 11 days to Jul 31, then 19 more days = **Aug 19**.
- The proclamation does not itself spell out this calculation.
Q2.uncertainty:
- The Annex II chapeau that 11056 amended is an image, so its wording cannot be checked.
- No refund mechanism is specified beyond 'standard procedures'.
- Recitals call the change a 3-day 'suspension' that 'lapsed', but the operative text simply sets a fixed new date; nothing in it is conditional.
- The 30-day arithmetic is inferred from the recital of the statute. Note also that Aug 22 is exactly 30 days after publication (Jul 23); no document says whether that mattered.

Q3.answer:
**(a) Shipments A–D** (customs value $30,000 each; 50% duty = $15,000):
- **A** (arrives Sep 10, entered Sep 14): may be imported, since the ban starts Sep 29. Section 338 duty $30,000 × 50% = **$15,000**.
- **B** (arrives Sep 27; withdrawn from warehouse Oct 5): may be withdrawn. It was imported before 12:01 a.m. Sep 29, so 11061 cl. (2) keeps it subject to the 50% duty: **$15,000**.
- **C** (arrives 11:30 p.m. Sep 28; entry 9:00 a.m. Sep 29): imported before the ban, so admissible. Entered after the ban date but covered by cl. (2): **$15,000**.
- **D** (arrives 12:30 a.m. Sep 29): excluded from importation under 11061 cl. (1). It cannot be entered, so there is no duty to compute.

**(b) Shipment E** (admitted to a foreign trade zone Sep 25; entry from the zone Oct 6):
- Under the scenario's definition, E was imported on Sep 25, before the ban. On that reading 11061 cl. (2) applies and it remains subject to the 50% duty on entry: **$15,000**.
- Under 11046 cl. (4), because it was admitted on or after the duty's effective date and is not eligible for domestic status, it had to be admitted in privileged foreign status.

**(c) Court holds the ban invalid for this beer:**
- 11061 cl. (9)(b): 'the 50 percent ad valorem duty imposed in Proclamation 11046 shall apply to the import to which the invalidated import ban ... had applied'.
- Duty = $30,000 × 50% = **$15,000** per shipment. Other bans and duties are unaffected.

**(d) Listed products not in the exclusion Annex:**
- No. 11061 cl. (3): 'Besides changing certain products from being subject to the additional ad valorem duties ... to being subject to the import ban ..., this proclamation does not otherwise affect the products' subject to the 11046 duties, as established in Proc. 11064.
- Those products stay at 50%, as modified by 11064.
Q3.uncertainty:
- 11061 does not address foreign trade zones. Whether admission to a zone counts as being 'imported' before Sep 29 is not stated; the answer for E relies on the scenario's definition of 'arrives'.
- 11061 cl. (2) names only goods 'imported, but not yet entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse'.

Q4.answer:
Each product has a customs value of $100,000 and a 25% section 232 duty.

**(a) Consumption entries on Sep 10, 2026:**
- **X (alcohol):** section 232 $100,000 × 25% = $25,000. Section 338 **$0**: 11046 cl. (2) excludes articles subject to section 232 duties.
- **Y (dairy):** section 232 $25,000. Section 338 **$0** under 11047 cl. (2).
- **Z (motor vehicles):** section 232 $25,000. Section 338 **$0** under 11048 cl. (2).

**(b) Consumption entries on Oct 1, 2026:**
- **X:** section 232 $25,000; section 338 $100,000 × 50% = **$50,000**. Total $75,000.
- **Y:** section 232 $25,000; section 338 **$0**. No dairy scope proclamation was published, so 11047 cl. (2) still controls.
- **Z:** section 232 $25,000; section 338 **$50,000**. Total $75,000. Z is on no Part A or Part B list, so 11076's changes do not reach it.

**(c) Controlling text:**
- **Exclusion of section 232 articles:** 11046 cl. (2) (91 FR 46641), 11047 cl. (2) (91 FR 46655) and 11048 cl. (2) (91 FR 46665) each say: 'The duties imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962'.
- **Stacking from Sep 15 (alcohol):** 11064 cl. (1) (91 FR 58332): 'The duties imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11046, as modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232 ... effective ... on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on September 15, 2026.'
- **Stacking from Sep 15 (motor vehicles):** 11065 cl. (1) (91 FR 58340) uses the same words for Proclamation 11048.
- **Restated for motor vehicles:** 11076 cl. (1) (91 FR 68862) restates the stacking from Oct 30.
- **Start date of the duties:** Aug 22 under 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790).
Q4.basis:
- Proclamations 11046, 11047 and 11048: cl. (2).
- Proclamations 11064 and 11065: cl. (1).
- Proclamation 11076: cl. (1).
- Proclamation 11056: cl. (1).
Q4.uncertainty:
- Proc. 11062 cl. (3) (91 FR 58320) refers to a 'Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... With Respect to Dairy)'. No such document appears in the Federal Register. If it existed and contained a stacking clause, Y would change.
- The stacking sentence in 11064 and 11065 sits in the same clause as the Part A/B changes. It is read here as applying to all products under the duty proclamation as modified, not only to Part A products.

Q5.answer:
**(a) Is the 50% duty owed at each time?** Times are: 3:00 p.m. Sep 14 / 12:01 a.m. Sep 15 / 4:00 p.m. Oct 29 / 12:01 a.m. Oct 30 / Nov 3.
- **P:** No / Yes / Yes / Yes / Yes. Added by 11065 Part A from 12:01 a.m. Sep 15; not on either 11076 list.
- **Q:** Yes / No / No / No / No. Dutiable from Aug 22 under 11048 Annex II; removed by 11065 Part B from Sep 15.
- **R:** Yes / Yes / Yes / No / No. Under 11048 Annex II; removed from 12:01 a.m. Oct 30 because 11076 Part A means 'shall no longer be subject'.
- **S:** No / No / No / Yes / Yes. Added by 11076 Part B from 12:01 a.m. Oct 30.
- Note that 11065 and 11076 use Part A and Part B in opposite senses. In 11065, Part A means added and Part B removed; in 11076, Part A means removed and Part B added.

**(b) Proc. 11076 dates and reach:**
- Signed Oct 23, 2026; filed with the Office of the Federal Register Oct 29, 2026 at 11:15 a.m.; published Oct 30, 2026 (91 FR 68861). It applies from 12:01 a.m. ET Oct 30, 2026 to goods entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption.
- The scope proclamations (11064, 11065, 11076) reach only entries made on or after their effective times. None provides for refunds; only 11056 cl. (4) has a refund clause.

**(c) Waiting period:**
- P: signed Sep 8, dutiable Sep 15 = **7 days**.
- S: signed Oct 23, dutiable Oct 30 = **7 days**.
- Both proclamations recite the section 338 limit of 'not to take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation' finding discrimination (11065 recital 8, 91 FR 58340; 11076 recital 9, 91 FR 68862). They also recite the authority to 'suspend, revoke, supplement, or amend' proclamations.
- Neither explains how adding products 7 days after signing fits the 30-day limit. The text is silent; the most that can be said is that it implicitly relies on the original Jul 20 finding plus the power to amend.
Q5.uncertainty:
- The documents give no explanation of the 30-day point.
- The product lists are images; the answers rely on the scenario's list assignments.

Q6.answer:
**(a) MFN rate 4%, customs value $100,000** (MFN duty $4,000 in every case):
1. **Switzerland** (12.5% net of MFN): 12.5% − 4% = 8.5% → section 301 $8,500. Total $4,000 + $8,500 = **$12,500**.
2. **Norway** (12.5%): $12,500. Total **$16,500**.
3. **United Kingdom** (10%): $10,000. Total **$14,000**.
4. **Germany** (EU, 10% net of MFN): 10% − 4% = 6% → $6,000. Total **$10,000**.
5. **Taiwan** (10% net of MFN): 6% → $6,000. Total **$10,000**.
6. **Türkiye** (12.5%): $12,500. Total **$16,500**.
7. **Japan** (12.5% net of MFN): 8.5% → $8,500. Total **$12,500**.
8. **Liechtenstein**: not one of the 60 investigated economies → $0. Total **$4,000**.
9. **Hong Kong** (12.5%): $12,500. Total **$16,500**.
10. **India** (10%): $10,000. Total **$14,000**.

**(b) Section 301 duty only, on $100,000:**
- Germany, MFN 12% (at or above 10%): **$0**.
- Japan, MFN 12%: 12.5% − 12% = 0.5% → **$500**.
- Taiwan, MFN exactly 10% ('greater than or equal to 10 percent'): **$0**.
- South Korea, MFN 10%: 12.5% − 10% = 2.5% → **$2,500**.
- Switzerland, MFN free: 12.5% − 0% → **$12,500**.

**(c) Changes from the June 2026 proposal:**
- **Germany (EU) and Taiwan:** proposed a flat 10%; adopted 10% net of MFN.
- **Japan and Switzerland:** proposed a flat 12.5% (the 'all other economies' group); adopted 12.5% net of MFN.
  - Stated reason: net-of-MFN tariffs 'would be consistent with their respective Agreements on Reciprocal Trade or similar arrangements and would be appropriate to encourage these economies to fulfill commitments' (memo recital, 91 FR 47719; Sec. 1(a)(ii), 47720).
- **India:** rate itself changed, 12.5% → 10%.
  - Stated reason: India adopted a forced-labor import prohibition after the June proposal; the higher rate is lowered 'to further encourage these economies to effectively enforce such prohibitions' (memo, 91 FR 47720; notice, 91 FR 47319; India determination, 91 FR 47324).
- **Unchanged:** Norway (12.5%), UK (10%, partial regime), Türkiye (12.5%) and Hong Kong (12.5%).
- **Liechtenstein:** not covered in either document.
Q6.basis:
- **Memorandum of Jul 23, 2026** (FR Doc. 2026-15274):
  - recitals (91 FR 47719–20);
  - Sec. 1(a)(i)–(iii) (91 FR 47720).
- **Notice of action** (FR Doc. 2026-15181):
  - Sec. II.A (91 FR 47320–21);
  - economy determinations, e.g. Norway (47326), Hong Kong (47324), Switzerland and Taiwan (47327), EU (47323).
- **June proposal** (FR Doc. 2026-11296): proposed rates (91 FR 34274).
Q6.uncertainty:
- The headings 9903.05.20–.84 and the economy lists in them are images. In particular it cannot be confirmed whether the HTSUS headings treat Liechtenstein together with Switzerland.
  - The section 232 proclamation 11032 does group Liechtenstein with Switzerland, but the section 301 action names only the 60 economies.
- Exempt-product lists are assumed not to apply.

Q7.answer:
**(a) France, 3¢/kg, 2,000 kg, value $12,000:**
- MFN duty = 2,000 × $0.03 = $60.
- Ad valorem equivalent = $60 ÷ $12,000 = 0.5%.
- Section 301 rate = 10% − 0.5% = 9.5%.
- Section 301 duty = $12,000 × 9.5% = **$1,140**.

**(b) 4% + 25¢/kg, 4,000 kg, value $20,000:**
- MFN duty = $20,000 × 4% = $800, plus 4,000 × $0.25 = $1,000, total $1,800.
- Ad valorem equivalent = $1,800 ÷ $20,000 = 9%.
- **Italy** (EU): 10% − 9% = 1% → **$200**.
- **Japan**: 12.5% − 9% = 3.5% → **$700**.
- **Brazil**: flat 12.5%, so the MFN rate is irrelevant → $20,000 × 12.5% = **$2,500**.

**(c) MFN duty $2,200 on value $20,000:**
- Ad valorem equivalent = $2,200 ÷ $20,000 = 11%.
- **Taiwan**: at or above 10% → **$0**.
- **Switzerland**: 12.5% − 11% = 1.5% → **$300**.

**(d) Where the rules are stated:**
- **Non-ad valorem rates:** U.S. note 52(k), in Annex I.A of the notice (91 FR 47394). For goods of an EU member state, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland or Taiwan subject to a specific or compound column 1-General rate, the ad valorem equivalent equals the duty payable divided by customs value. The note gives a 50¢/kg ÷ $10 = 5% example.
- **Equivalent rate below the cap:** the closing paragraphs of note 52(k) say the sum is 10% (headings 9903.05.39 and .76) or 12.5% (9903.05.49, .71 and .74).
- **Equivalent rate at or above the cap (zero section 301 duty):** the readable note text does not state this. It is stated in:
  - memo Sec. 1(a)(ii) (91 FR 47720);
  - the notice's Sec. II.A (91 FR 47320–21);
  - the economy determinations' 'For greater certainty' sentences (EU, 47323; South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan, 47327).
- The heading descriptions that presumably carry the zero rate (e.g. 9903.05.38, .48, .70, .73, .75) are images.
Q7.uncertainty:
- The memo and preamble speak of the 'MFN tariff' without explaining how to convert specific rates. Only note 52(k) does that, and it applies only to the five named economies.
- The image headings may contain further detail.

Q8.answer:
The Dominican Republic rate is 12.5%, so the duty when owed is $80,000 × 12.5% = **$10,000**.

**(a) Shipments:**
1. Loaded Jul 22, entered Jul 29: **$10,000**. The in-transit exception requires entry before 12:01 a.m. Jul 28.
2. Same sailing, entered 3:00 p.m. Jul 27: **$0**. Loaded on a vessel before 12:01 a.m. Jul 24, in transit on the final mode, and entered before 12:01 a.m. Jul 28.
3. Same sailing, entered 12:01 a.m. Jul 28: **$10,000**. Not 'before' 12:01 a.m. Jul 28.
4. Loaded 6:00 a.m. Jul 24, entered Jul 27: **$10,000**. Loaded after 12:01 a.m. Jul 24, so no exception.
5. Entered Jul 23: **$0**. Before the duties applied.
6. Bonded warehouse, withdrawn Jul 26: **$10,000**. Withdrawal on or after Jul 24; the goods were not in transit on a vessel.
7. Air freight, loaded 9:00 p.m. Jul 23, entered Jul 25: **$10,000**. The exception covers only goods 'loaded onto a vessel'.

**(b) Where the in-transit rule is stated:**
- Only in the DATES line of the USTR notice (FR Doc. 2026-15181, 91 FR 47318): 'goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in transit on the final mode of transit before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, and entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026, shall not be subject to such additional duty.'
- Annex I.A (91 FR 47335–36) and U.S. note 52 do not repeat it. The memorandum is silent.

**(c) Dates:**
- Memorandum signed Jul 23, 2026.
- Duties apply to entries or withdrawals on or after 12:01 a.m. ET Jul 24, 2026 (DATES line; Annex I.A).
- The notice of action and the memorandum were both published Jul 28, 2026 (91 FR 47318; 91 FR 47717). The duties applied before publication.

**(d) Patented pharmaceutical, heading 9903.04.62:**
- Entered **Jul 30**: $80,000 × 12.5% = **$10,000**. Not yet exempt.
- Entered **Aug 3**: **$0**. Annex I.B, effective for entries on or after 12:01 a.m. Jul 31, 2026, adds item (8), 'patented pharmaceutical articles provided for in headings 9903.04.60–9903.04.66', to note 52(f) and amends heading 9903.05.90 (91 FR 47394).
Q8.uncertainty:
- Whether 'vessel' could be read to include aircraft is not addressed; the plain text covers vessels only.
- Any section 232 pharmaceutical duty on 9903.04.62 goods is outside this question.

Q9.answer:
**(a) Thailand, heading 9802.00.80:**
- Dutiable base = $100,000 − $35,000 U.S. components = $65,000.
- $65,000 × 12.5% = **$8,125**.

**(b) Israel, subheading 9802.00.50:**
- Duty applies only to the value of the repairs: $6,000 × 12.5% = **$750**.

**(c) Mexico, MFN 5%, value $50,000:**
- (i) Entered free under USMCA: **$0** (note 52(h)).
- (ii) No USMCA claim: $50,000 × 10% = **$5,000**.

**(d) Japanese passenger car, heading 9903.94.01:** **$0** (note 52(f)(2)).

**(e) Brazil, section 232 duty under an unlisted chapter 99 heading:** $100,000 × 12.5% = **$12,500**. Note 52(a) says products remain subject to any other subchapter III/IV additional duty, and only the headings listed in 52(f) are exempt.

**(f) Proposal vs adopted text:**
- **June 2026 proposal:** the action would not cover 'informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage; all articles and parts of articles that are subject to section 232 tariffs' (Annex A note, 91 FR 34276; also 34274: 'informational materials (e.g., books), donations, and accompanied baggage').
- **Adopted note 52:**
  - **Section 232:** exempts only the articles in the specified section 232 headings: aluminum, steel and copper and derivative headings 9903.82.02 and .04–.26; listed auto and auto-parts headings; wood; medium- and heavy-duty vehicles; semiconductors; and, from Jul 31, patented pharmaceuticals (52(f); Annex I.B). Otherwise 52(a) makes section 301 duties apply on top of other additional duties.
  - **Accompanied baggage:** excludes only 'products for personal use included in accompanied baggage' (52(a)).
  - **Informational materials and donations:** the adopted text is silent; it does not exempt them.
- **How the notice describes it:** the preamble restates the proposed exemptions (91 FR 47318) and says all proposed exemptions were kept except non-pharmaceutical chemicals (47330). The operative note does not bear that out.
Q9.basis:
- Notice FR Doc. 2026-15181: U.S. note 52(a), (f), (h) (91 FR 47352, 47362–63); Annex I.B (47394); Sec. I and III.C (47318, 47330).
- Proposal FR Doc. 2026-11296 (91 FR 34274, 34276).
- Mexico 10% and Thailand, Brazil and Israel 12.5%: determinations at 91 FR 47324–28.
Q9.uncertainty:
- The chapter 98 exemption in note 52(a) might cover some donations or informational materials entered under a chapter 98 provision. Books classified in chapter 49 are not exempt by any readable text.
- The image lists in 52(b) may contain further items.

Q10.answer:
**Scenario 1: Canadian aluminum extrusions**, value $200,000, MFN 3%, no USMCA claim.

**(a) Entry Sep 10, 2026:**
- MFN: $200,000 × 3% = $6,000.
- Section 232: $200,000 × 50% = $100,000.
- Section 338: $0. Proc. 11048 cl. (2) excludes section 232 articles.
- Section 301: $0. Note 52(f)(1) exempts derivative aluminum articles under 9903.82.02.
- **Total $106,000.**

**(b) Entry Sep 16, 2026:**
- MFN: $6,000.
- Section 232: $100,000.
- Section 338: $200,000 × 50% = $100,000. 11065 cl. (1) applies the duty in addition to section 232 from Sep 15.
- Section 301: $0.
- **Total $206,000.**

**Scenario 2: Canadian rye whisky**, value $60,000, MFN free, on the exclusion Annex.

**(c) Sep 1, 2026, entered free under USMCA:**
- Section 338: $60,000 × 50% = $30,000. The section 338 proclamations contain no USMCA exception.
- Section 301: $0. Note 52(g) exempts products of Canada entered free under USMCA.
- **Total $30,000.**

**(d) Sep 1, 2026, no USMCA claim:**
- Section 338: $30,000.
- Section 301: $60,000 × 10% = $6,000.
- **Total $36,000.**

**(e) Arrives Oct 2, 2026:**
- Excluded from importation under 11061 cl. (1) (goods imported on or after 12:01 a.m. Sep 29). It cannot be entered, so there is no duty.
- If the ban were invalidated as to it, 11061 cl. (9)(b) would apply the 50% duty ($30,000). Section 301 would then be $6,000 without a USMCA claim, or $0 with one.

**(f) Other Canada duties in September 2026:**
- **IEEPA 'northern border' duties:** none. Executive Order 14193 (FR Doc. 2025-02406) was amended by EO 14197, EO 14231 (USMCA goods exempt from Mar 7, 2025) and EO 14325 (35% from Aug 1, 2025). EO 14389, 'Ending Certain Tariff Actions' (signed Feb 20, 2026; FR Doc. 2026-03832, 91 FR 9437), declared that the IEEPA duties under EO 14193 'shall no longer be in effect' and directed that collection end as soon as practicable.
- **10% temporary import surcharge:** none. Proclamation 11012 under section 122 (FR Doc. 2026-03824) applied from 12:01 a.m. EST Feb 24, 2026 'through 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 24, 2026' (cl. (7), 91 FR 9343). It had also excluded USMCA goods and section 232 articles (91 FR 9341–42, cl. (4)).
- No extension appears in the Federal Register.
Q10.uncertainty:
- The section 232 rate and base are taken from the scenario.
- The section 338 proclamations do not say expressly whether the duty applies to USMCA-qualifying goods; no exception appears in the readable text.

Q11.answer:
Discrepancies found:

**1. A dairy scope proclamation that does not exist.**
- Proc. 11062 cl. (3) (91 FR 58320) says the ban does not otherwise affect products 'as further established in the Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... With Respect to Dairy)'.
- The only Sep 8 scope proclamations are 11064 (alcohol, 91 FR 58331) and 11065 (motor vehicles, 91 FR 58339). No dairy scope proclamation is published.

**2. Where Proc. 11056 changed the date vs where the date is printed.**
- 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790) changes the date by amending 'the chapeau of Annex II' of 11046–11048, deleting 'August 19, 2026'.
- The Aug 19 date appears in the operative clauses (1) and (3) of each duty proclamation (e.g. 91 FR 46641, 46655, 46665). Those clauses are left unamended and are reconciled only by 11056's general supersession clause (5).

**3. 'Suspension that lapsed' vs a fixed new date.**
- 11061, 11062, 11063, 11064, 11065 and 11076 recite that 11056 'temporarily suspended for 3 days' the duties and that 'at 12:01 a.m. ... August 22, 2026, the 3-day suspension ... lapsed' because Canada reneged on Aug 21 (e.g. 91 FR 58311, 58331, 68861).
- 11056's title and recitals 4–5 likewise speak of 'suspending for a period of 3 days' (54790).
- 11056 cl. (1) does not suspend anything conditionally. It simply makes Aug 22 'the effective date'. The duties began because of that date, not because of Canada's conduct.
- The same recitals also describe the duties as imposed 'effective August 19, 2026' (e.g. 58311 recital 1), the date 11056 replaced.

**4. How the memorandum describes the proposed textile mechanism.**
- The memorandum recital (91 FR 47719) says the proposal would let textiles 'enter the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate'.
- The June proposal (91 FR 34274) and the notice's summary of it (91 FR 47318) say 'a reduced Section 301 tariff rate'.

**5. Annex A exemptions said to be kept vs the adopted note.**
- Notice Sec. III.C (91 FR 47330): USTR 'determined to exempt all of the products proposed for exemption in Annex A ... except the non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products', and 'determined not to remove additional products'.
- The proposal's Annex A also exempted 'informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage; all articles and parts of articles that are subject to section 232 tariffs' (91 FR 34276).
- Adopted note 52(a) and (f) (91 FR 47352, 47362–63) keep only personal-use accompanied baggage. They exempt only listed section 232 headings, and make other products subject to 'any additional duty' in subchapters III/IV. There is no exemption for informational materials or donations.

**6. Whether all economies 'failed to impose' a prohibition.**
- The notice's account of the June 2 determinations (91 FR 47318) says six economies (Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan) 'have failed to effectively enforce' a prohibition, which implies they impose one.
- The next sentence says 'All of the investigated economies have failed to impose a forced labor import prohibition and to effectively enforce such a prohibition'.
- The proposal (91 FR 34274) describes those six as economies 'that impose a forced labor import prohibition'.

**7. Exemption category (c): 'or at reasonable prices'.**
- The memorandum recital lists category (c) as products that cannot be produced 'in sufficient quantities or at reasonable prices' (47719).
- The memorandum's operative Sec. 1(b)(iii) omits 'or at reasonable prices' (47720–21).
- The notice says its exemptions follow 'the specific direction of the President' but uses the broader wording (47319, 47321), while quoting the narrower Sec. 1(b)(iii) at 47320.

**8. Severability quotations.**
- Notice Sec. IV (91 FR 47335) quotes the memorandum as saying 'each tariff directed in this memorandum that is implemented—with any combinations of exemptions' and 'should be treated invalid'.
- Memo Sec. 4(d)–(e) (91 FR 47722–23) reads 'each tariff action directed ...', 'any combination of exemptions' and 'treated as invalid'. These are minor misquotations.

**9. The 'September 1' textile quota date.**
- The memorandum recital says establishing the quotas 'will be feasible by September 1, 2026' (47720).
- Operative Sec. 2(a)–(b) sets no date: 'As soon as the Trade Representative determines that it is feasible'.
- This is a recital vs operative difference within the memorandum, noted here for completeness.

Q13.answer:
Section 232 duty only. Customs value $200,000 per unit.

**(a) USMCA claim; U.S. parts $60,000:**
- Non-U.S. content = $200,000 − $60,000 = $140,000.
- $140,000 × 25% = $35,000, which is 17.5% of value.
- The floor is 15% of total value = $200,000 × 15% = $30,000. The floor is not binding.
- **Duty $35,000.** This is also lower than the 25% full-value rate ($50,000), and cl. (3)(b) applies the lowest applicable rate.

**(b) USMCA claim; no U.S. content:** $200,000 × 25% = **$50,000**.

**(c) No USMCA qualification:** clause (2)(d) is unavailable and Canada is not among the (2)(b) jurisdictions. $200,000 × 25% = **$50,000**.

**(d) Product of Japan, MFN 2.5%:**
- Clause (2)(b): 15% − 2.5% = 12.5%.
- $200,000 × 12.5% = **$25,000**.

**(e) USMCA claim; U.S. parts $20,000; $30,000 of U.S.-smelted aluminum inside a Canadian-made part:**
- Only 'parts produced in the United States' count as U.S. content. U.S.-smelted aluminum in a Canadian part does not.
- Non-U.S. content = $200,000 − $20,000 = $180,000.
- $180,000 × 25% = $45,000, which is 22.5% and above the 15% floor.
- The 10% rate in cl. (2)(c) is unavailable because most of the metal was melted or smelted abroad (the 85% test in cl. (4) is not met).
- **Duty $45,000.**

**(f) As (e) but entered Oct 6, 2026:** **$45,000**. The same rules apply throughout Jun 8, 2026 to Dec 31, 2027, and no change between Oct 6 and Oct 20 appears in the Federal Register.

**(g) USMCA claim; U.S. parts $140,000:**
- Non-U.S. content = $60,000; $60,000 × 25% = $15,000, which is 7.5%.
- The 15% floor applies: $200,000 × 15% = **$30,000**.

**(h) Duration:**
- Treatment under cl. (2) applies to entries from 12:01 a.m. EDT Jun 8, 2026 'until 11:59 p.m. eastern standard time on December 31, 2027'.
- From 12:01 a.m. EST Jan 1, 2028, Annex I-C products bear 'the rates set out in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021' (Proc. 11032 cl. (3)(a)).
Q13.uncertainty:
- The floor's mechanics are 'as detailed in Annex IV', which is an image.
- Commerce guidance on assessing 'U.S. content' is referenced but not published in the Federal Register.
- Nothing found explains why the Oct 6 and Oct 20 dates would differ.

Q14.answer:
**1. Incorrect.**
- The 'September 1, 2026' date appears only in a memorandum recital: the Trade Representative informed the President that the quotas 'will be feasible by September 1, 2026' (91 FR 47720).
- Operative Sec. 2(a)–(b) says 'As soon as the Trade Representative determines that it is feasible'. Sec. 2(c) imposes the 10% rate until then.
- The notice says 'establish, when feasible' (47318, 47321). Neither document sets a deadline.

**2. Incorrect.**
- USTR received 'over 1,600 written comments' and testimony from 'over 100 witnesses' (memo, 47719; notice, 47319 and 47328).

**3. Incorrect in part.**
- The memorandum and notice name seven economies that acted after the proposal: Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka and Trinidad and Tobago adopted prohibitions, and Jordan made an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade commitment. All are 'tariffed at the 10 percent rate' (memo, 47720; notice, 47319).
- But Cambodia and Guatemala had already been proposed at 10% because of their reciprocal trade agreement commitments (proposal, 91 FR 34274; memo recital, 47719).
- Jordan moved because of an agreement commitment, not a ban.
- So five moved from 12.5% to 10% (Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago), and only four of them because of a ban.

**4. Incorrect.**
- USTR 'determined not to remove these products from the list of exempted products', listing beef and avocados among them. It cited section 301(c)(3)(B) in rejecting the forced-labor linkage argument (notice, 47331).

**5. Incorrect.**
- The EU (Annex II Part C), Switzerland (Part D) and Taiwan (Part K) have their own lists (47323, 47327).
- Japan and South Korea are net-of-MFN but are exempt only under Annex I and Annex II Part A (47324, 47327).
- Memo Sec. 1(b)(v) names the EU, Switzerland and Taiwan, not Japan or Korea (47721).

**6. Partly correct.**
- The 471 figure is right: 'an additional 471 products' (47331).
- The sugar point is not. The notice says 'certain sugar and sugar containing products', and its discussion is of 'in-quota imports' (47331–32). It does not say all sugar products.

**7. Incorrect.**
- No overall cap is stated.
- The cap applies only to MFN plus the section 301 duty for the EU and Taiwan (10%) and Japan, Korea and Switzerland (12.5%) (memo Sec. 1(a)(ii), 47720).
- Note 52(a) makes section 301 products also subject to other additional duties (47352).
- Other economies pay MFN plus 10% or 12.5%.

**8. Correct.**
- The notice states that such products 'only may be admitted as privileged foreign status ... effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed', unless eligible for domestic status (47321). This is preamble text; note 52 does not repeat it.

**9. Correct, as stated intent.**
- Memo Sec. 4(e): 'The applicable tariff action ... should apply to imports to which the invalidated exemption ... applied before its invalidation' (47723).
- Notice Sec. IV says the same: the 'tariff action ... would apply' (47335).

**10. Partly correct.**
- The notice says so: USTR exempted 'all of the products proposed for exemption in Annex A ... except the non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products' (47330).
- But the operative note goes further. The proposal's Annex A also exempted informational materials, donations and all section 232 articles (91 FR 34276). Adopted note 52(a) and (f) keep only personal-use accompanied baggage and listed section 232 headings (47352, 47362–63).
Q14.uncertainty:
- Annex lists are images, so the exact composition of the 471 products and of the sugar items cannot be checked.
- For item 10, the scope of the proposal's 'Annex A' as a matter of wording is arguable: the informational-materials and section 232 exemptions sat in the Annex A note rather than in its list.

Q15.answer:
Customs value $100,000, all aluminum. N = goods do not qualify for USMCA; U = goods qualify and are entered with a USMCA claim.

**1. Feb 10, 2025 — N $0; U $0.**
- Section 232: Canada was exempt until Mar 12, 2025 (Proc. 10895).
- IEEPA (EO 14193): paused until 12:01 a.m. Mar 4, 2025 by EO 14197.

**2. Mar 6, 2025 — N $25,000; U $25,000.**
- IEEPA 25%: $100,000 × 25% = $25,000 for both.
- The USMCA exemption (EO 14231 Sec. 2) applies only to entries from 12:01 a.m. Mar 7, 2025.
- Section 232: Canada still exempt until Mar 12.

**3. Mar 10, 2025 — N $25,000; U $0.**
- N: IEEPA 25% = $25,000.
- U: IEEPA not owed (USMCA, EO 14231).
- Section 232: not yet in force for Canada.

**4. Mar 14, 2025 — N $25,000; U $25,000.**
- N: IEEPA $25,000. Section 232 25% not owed: under EO 14289 Sec. 3(a)(ii) as first issued, an article subject to the IEEPA Canada duty 'shall not be subject' to the aluminum section 232 duty, retroactive to entries on or after Mar 4, 2025 (Sec. 5).
- U: IEEPA not owed; section 232 25% = $25,000 (Proc. 10895, from Mar 12).
- Reciprocal duty (EO 14257): not applicable to Canada (Sec. 3(d)).

**5. Jun 3, 2025 — N $25,000; U $25,000.**
- Same as item 4. The 50% section 232 rate starts Jun 4.

**6. Jun 10, 2025 — N $50,000; U $50,000.**
- Section 232 50% (Proc. 10947 cl. (1), from 12:01 a.m. Jun 4): $100,000 × 50% = $50,000.
- IEEPA not owed: 10947 cl. (5) reversed the rule in EO 14289 so that section 232 articles are not subject to the IEEPA Canada duty, effective Jun 4.

**7. Aug 5, 2025 — N $50,000; U $50,000.**
- Section 232 $50,000.
- IEEPA 35% (EO 14325, from Aug 1) not owed, under the same reversed non-stacking rule; for U it is also not owed because of USMCA.

**8. Mar 2, 2026 — N $50,000; U $50,000.**
- Section 232 $50,000.
- IEEPA duties ended by EO 14389 (Feb 20, 2026).
- Section 122 surcharge of 10% (Proc. 11012, from Feb 24) not owed: cl. (4) and para. (k) exclude section 232 articles; for U, para. (l) also excludes USMCA goods.

**9. Jun 10, 2026 — N $50,000; U $50,000.**
- Section 232 at 50% on full value (Proc. 11021 cl. (1), (2)(a), from Apr 6, 2026). Annex I-A of 11021 carries no USMCA reduction; Proc. 11032 applies only to Annex I-C.
- Surcharge not owed (section 232 article). The section 301 and section 338 duties were not yet in force.

**10. Jul 27, 2026 — N $50,000; U $50,000.**
- Section 232 $50,000.
- Section 301 (from Jul 24) not owed: note 52(f)(1) exempts heading 9903.82.02; for U, 52(g) also applies.
- Surcharge expired 12:01 a.m. Jul 24. Section 338 not yet effective (Aug 22).

**11. Aug 25, 2026 — N $50,000; U $50,000.**
- Section 232 $50,000.
- Section 338 not owed: Proc. 11048 cl. (2) excludes section 232 articles.
- Section 301 not owed (52(f)(1)).

**12. Sep 14, 2026 — N $50,000; U $50,000.** Same as item 11.

**13. Sep 16, 2026 — N $100,000; U $100,000.**
- Section 232: $50,000.
- Section 338: $100,000 × 50% = $50,000. Proc. 11065 cl. (1) applies the duty in addition to section 232 from Sep 15. No USMCA exception appears.
- Section 301: not owed (52(f)(1)).

**14. Nov 10, 2026 — N $100,000; U $100,000.**
- Same as item 13. The extrusions are not on Proc. 11076's Part A or Part B lists.
Q15.uncertainty:
- **IEEPA validity:** EO 14389 ends the IEEPA duties 'in light of recent events' but does not say they were invalid from the start. If a court held them unlawful (the Federal Register does not say so), the IEEPA amounts for items 2–5 would not be legally owed. In that case, for items 4–5 Case N, the 25% section 232 duty ($25,000) would arguably apply instead, because EO 14289's non-stacking turns on the article being 'subject to' the IEEPA duty.
- **Proc. 10106:** Proc. 10895's text indicates Canada's aluminum exemption ran until Mar 12, 2025; the details of 10106 were not read.
- **Content basis before Apr 6, 2026:** treated as the full value here, because all of the value is aluminum.
- **Section 338 and USMCA:** the section 338 proclamations do not mention USMCA.
